title: Call parameter schema authoring guide and runtime hygiene runbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: define a single, pragmatic JSON-schema-based format and a deterministic runtime validation + recovery protocol for tool/function call parameters. This ticket captures the authoring guidance for model/tool integrators, the runtime validation flow (including safe coercions and KV/cache interactions), and a minimal error taxonomy with stable error codes we can expose in logs, console UI, and client SDKs. We must also document compatibility rules so newer schemas do not break older clients and so the runtime can perform graceful degradation when strict validation would otherwise reject a request.
runtime_validation_flow: 1) Fast pre-parse: ensure JSON payload is syntactically valid; attach a short parse error with byte offset if not. 2) Coercion pass (opt-in per-route): apply safe coercions: numeric strings -> numbers, boolean strings ("true"/"false") -> booleans, drop nulls for non-nullable fields only when 'coerceNulls' route flag is enabled. Coercions must be recorded in an 'applied_coercions' trace for debugging. 3) Schema validation pass: run constrained JSON Schema profile; accumulate all validation errors instead of failing fast. 4) Recovery policy: if schema errors are only missing optional fields or additionalProperties and 'allow_additional_properties' route flag is enabled, accept with warnings. If required fields missing, return structured validation failure. 5) Fallback routing: when validation fails but the route has a compatible alternate model variant (e.g., relaxed-schema model), auto-reroute with a documented event and telemetry increment. 6) Final: emit structured outcome object to caller and console including stable error_code, human_message, corrected_payload (if coercions applied), and validation_details (only in logs and admin console).
error_taxonomy: We will publish a small set of stable error codes (strings) used across runtime, SDKs, and console: 1) CALL_PARSE_ERROR - JSON parsing issues; payload malformed. 2) CALL_PARAM_MISSING - required parameter(s) absent. 3) CALL_PARAM_TYPE - value type mismatch (after coercion attempt). 4) CALL_PARAM_CONSTRAINT - constraints violated (min/max/format/enum). 5) CALL_PARAM_ADDITIONAL - extra properties present and additionalProperties=false. 6) CALL_PARAM_COERCED - successful coercions were applied (NOT an error, recorded as info). 7) CALL_PARAM_RECOVERED - validation failed but runtime applied recovery policy (e.g., removed unknown fields) and proceeded. 8) CALL_PARAM_FATAL - validation failure that cannot be recovered; request rejected. Each code is accompanied by a numeric telemetry tag for ingestion into metrics pipeline.
human_messages_mapping: Mapping principles: 1) short (<=120 chars) human_message for end user/client SDKs, 2) verbose developer_hint for admin console and logs, 3) suggested_fix examples when available. Examples as single-line entries: CALL_PARAM_MISSING -> human_message: 'Missing required parameter: user_id' ; developer_hint: 'Add user_id (uuid) to the top-level object. Example: "user_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6"' CALL_PARAM_TYPE -> human_message: 'Parameter limit must be an integer' ; developer_hint: 'limit received as "10" (string). Enable route coercion or send as number.' CALL_PARAM_ADDITIONAL -> human_message: 'Unexpected parameter: foo' ; developer_hint: 'Parameter "foo" is not in the schema. Either remove it or set route to allow additional properties.'
compatibility_strategy: - Schema versioning: every schema gets a semver-like id in metadata (x-schema-version). Runtime will accept payloads that claim older versions and apply a compatibility adapter chain. - Deprecation headers: when schema tightens (a required field added or additionalProperties flips to false), runtime emits a deprecation warning header (X-Call-Schema-Deprecation) to callers for 30 days before strict enforcement. - Relaxed fallback: maintain a 'compatibility mode' model variant that will be used automatically when strict validation fails but the route is marked 'auto_fallback=true'. - Migration runbook: document how to roll a schema change using canary, A/B, and gradual required flag flips.
implementation_notes: Tasks: 1) schema parser + constrained validator lib (go/python) - Diego to prototype (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4271). 2) SDK mapping for stable error codes - Ajay to add to js/python SDKs. 3) Console: show 'validation_details' and applied_coercions in request view - UX ticket PM-4021. 4) Telemetry: numeric tags and counters for each error code - infra: add to snowplow/metrics pipeline. 5) E2E tests: property-based tests for coercion and recovery. Blockers: need final decision on allowed 'format' set and whether to allow 'oneOf' in nested helpers.
acceptance_criteria: - Constrained JSON schema parser implemented and integration tests passing (unit + property). - Runtime returns structured error payloads with stable error_code field for all validation outcomes. - SDKs map error_code -> human_message consistently. - Console shows validation_details for admin access and marks requests where coercions were applied. - Backcompat runbook written and reviewed by Security and Platform teams. - PRs merged: runtime prototype, SDK changes, console feature flag.
